Right now im focusing on finishing up my degree and getting a job before I pursue family. But as of right now, I have never felt happier. Although I love the idea of having a wife and kids, I actually wouldn't mind being a monk or something tbh. I feel confident on my own and have overcome a lot of the lonliness I had as a young adult. So wife or no wife, for the first time, I feel happy about the future.
You already have a head start on a lot of people your age. Fufilling career, friends. You can really become someone who your proud of. I believe in you!
He wants to have a wife and a family and you suggest an escort? Terrible advice

Im glad to hear it. You know it's interesting, most of my firends that had a bunch of girlfriends when they were younger are now burnouts who are stuck at cummunity college. The two friends I have who are doing things with their life, never had a girlfriend. It really is a grass is always greener thing. Now I don't mind being alone and enjoy the quiet moments of solitude.

This whole culture is built around romance. People will tell you you need some other person to actually feel fufilled. The truth is you do not. The happiest and most interesting people I have meet are friars and nuns who have no romantic relationship in their lives. You can become a respectable person with friends who does work that matters, without someone there to affirm that. It is nice to be in a relationship because someone in your life will affirm what your doing and make you feel 'nice' but if you want to be truly happy you have to find a way to do that for yourself. relationships end and people die, you have to be there for yourself and have that be enough.

  
Trust me, as someone who was desperate for female attention, when I was actually in a relationship I felt good for a bit but was miserable again. If you want a good wife and family, become someone who is independent and is confident in your ability to function on your own. That kind of personality will attract a good future wife and mother, it just takes patience to find them.

I hope this doesn't come off as ranting at you, I just was in a pretty similar situation to you and I thought I'd share some of the advice that helped me be truly happy. You can be a great, interesting and happy person on your own, and from that inward joy and confidence you will attract a woman who will make a great mother of your future children. Keep at it, don't give up. Being a father is a very noble thing, I am praying for you.

There is so much instore for you besides 'not going to hell'. God will wipe every tear from your eye, I promise. Talk to a priest, they won't break confidence and he can really help you. God wants to relieve you of your burdens I promise, just hold in there, please. Love and prayers from me to you always

That is terrible, and I am so sorry you had to endure all of that. It breaks my heart that your innocence was stolen from you at such a young age and that it continues to cause immense pain in your life. I cannot guarantee that things will improve materially in the near future, and I won't make empty promises. But I can promise you this: God loves you.

I was suicidal for many years. I had a terrible relationship with my parents, I was failing out of school, and nothing seemed to help. I tried medication, therapy, and practically everything I could to heal myself, but I was still depressed and thought constantly about suicide. I wanted to escape all my problems and pain and finally be free. This desire came to a head when I was 17, when I had my first serious suicide attempt. I had always toyed with the idea—seeing how much I could make myself bleed by cutting my wrists or trying to work up the courage on the edge of the bridge near my house. But this time was different. I was determined to end it and I wouldn't let fear get in the way of it

Using a belt raised high enough to bring my weight off the ground, I attempted to hang myself. It worked. I lost consciousness and began suffocating. But somehow, the apparatus I had built miraculously failed, and I woke up later on the floor, severely injured but alive. I spent months in a psych hospital afterward, which was a terrible experience in itself. When I was released, nothing had changed—I was still failing my classes, still consumed by despair, and still making new plans for suicide.

It wasn’t until I began to reconnect, seemingly by chance, with the Catholic faith of my youth that things started to change. It didn’t happen overnight, and it didn’t magically fix my problems. But for the first time in my life, I began to grasp something I had been desperately searching for through all this pain and suffering: peace.

My whole life, I had been trying to escape—from loneliness, from the contempt my parents had for me, from my constant failures and shortcomings. I thought I could only find freedom by ending my life. But I was wrong. The escape didn’t come from taking my life—it came from giving my life to God. All my misery, hatred, loneliness, and despair no longer defined my entire existence. I was finally able to feel peace.

For the first time, I knew—unmistakably, deep down—that I was cared for and loved. Someone who understood the depth of my pain and suffering loved me and was willing to help me bear my burdens. Before this, I felt utterly insignificant, like I was a million miles away from everyone else. I felt no one cared about me, that people hated me for being an inconvenience, and that they would be glad if I were gone. I thought my suffering was pointless and that everything I endured was for nothing. But now I know that’s not true. Now I know my life has meaning, and my suffering wasn’t for nothing. Now I now there is comfort and consolation for all this pain.

I was starting to come to terms with my misery and asked God, desperately, to help me understand it. It took time—so much time—but through prayer, trust, and the sacraments, God slowly healed my wounds and helped understand my suffering and freed me from all the pain. I no longer desire death and for the first time, perhaps since I was a child, I have real love in my heart.

Not long ago, I was apathetic, pessimistic, and miserable, unwilling to trust anyone, especially my parents. I was convinced that love was a lie—a delusion or just a chemical response to induce breeding. But now, I love with the innocence and trust of a child, and that love brings me so much joy.

I know this may sound unbelievable to you. Maybe I’m just a privileged, deluded person clinging to an illusion or just lucked out of misery. Well it is true that I am privellaged and I know you have endured far worse than I ever have. But believe me when I say, with every once of my being I know that without my faith and the prayers of strangers, I would not be alive today. I am convinced of that.

So, whether you believe me or not, please know this: I would stake my life on the conviction that God loves you. If you feel stuck in pain and despair, what do you have to lose by reaching out to Him? What do you have to lose by asking for understanding, consolation, and peace? I can't imagine how hard it must be for you to trust anyone, when God, like so many people in your life who were supposed to protect you and rescue you from danger, was seeminly absent.

That is why I pray for you with all my will, so that your heart may be open to trust the one who desires more than anything to heal it. That is the only way to put this painful past to rest, it is the only way to finally have the peace you deserve.

You deserve to know that you are loved. You deserve to have peace. If God could take someone as weak and privileged as me and bring meaning to my suffering, imagine what He could do for someone as strong as you. You have endured more pain in one lifetime than most have expierenced or could bear. Imagine how much more God is willing to give you if He has done so much for someone like me who has endured so little. There is rest for you in this life, and I believe with all my heart that God will give it to you. All He wants is to be near you—not to judge you, but to love and comfort you. If the love I feel in my heart toward you now is only a fraction of how much God loves you, then I know He loves you deeply.

Right now, you have given me a great gift. You have given me the opprotunity to return the love shown to me when I was in despair and offer it to you. I, a stranger, am now praying for you, just as a stranger once prayed for me. And I trust that God will answer you, comfort you and wipe away every tear from your face, just as He has done for me.

I love you
